extracted.intended_audience: federal policymakers, National Academy/National Research Council administrators, state selection committees, and education/military officials implementing postwar science scholarship and fellowship programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for establishing, allocating, selecting, administering, and terminating National Science Reserve scholarships and fellowships, and related measures for discovering and training scientific talent (including veterans and servicemembers).

rubrics_metrics.name: State allocation of scholarships
rubrics_metrics.description: The 6,000 proposed scholarships should be assigned to the States on the basis of the number of their secondary school graduates of the previous year as related to the national total of such graduates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation example: based on 1939-40 figures (table in Appendix C). Scholarships also intended to be available to Territories and Insular Possessions; inclusion of these would decrease State quotas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative organization and operating agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend that a National Scientific Research Foundation, or similar organization, make arrangements for choosing Scholars and Fellows through the National Academy of Sciences, with operation entrusted to the Academy’s operating agency, the National Research Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More precise details of the Academy’s participation and operational means are stated in Appendix C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of expert advisory bodies and central staff
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure the fairest, most effective and most up-to-date methods of selection, advisory bodies expert in such matters must be set up and a central administrative staff chosen for ability and integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No existing national science organization has shown itself as well-equipped for such advisory functions as the National Academy; the central staff will cooperate with advisory bodies to prepare tests and evaluate applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: State selection committee composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Committees of selection in each State should consist of five members: three scientists (one to serve as chairman); one member of a college or university faculty trained and experienced in selection and guidance; and one representative of secondary education within the State (usually a secondary school principal or high school supervisor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one of the scientists should be from agriculture or from industry within the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationwide testing and data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative staff, in cooperation with advisory bodies, would prepare tests in accordance with the best thought upon such matters; these tests would be given to all applicants and test reports sent to the national organization for evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The national staff would also collect other relevant data and judgments concerning each applicant to support certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of qualified candidates to States
rubrics_metrics.description: Based upon tests and other material the national staff would certify to the State Committees a number of qualified candidates equal to twice the State’s quota.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification is subject to the provision that no applicants shall be certified who do not attain a certain minimum national standard; dossiers of certified candidates are sent to State committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: State committees make final selections
rubrics_metrics.description: State committees would have the responsibility of making the final selections of the Scholars up to the number of the State’s quota.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State committees decide among the nationally certified dossiers to fill their allocated scholarships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum national standard for certification
rubrics_metrics.description: No applicants shall be certified who do not attain a certain minimum national standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum standard applied nationally by the national staff before forwarding candidate dossiers to State committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole basis of selection is merit
rubrics_metrics.description: For both scholarships and fellowships, the sole basis of selection should be merit, without regard to sex, race, color, creed, or need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection procedures and committees must ensure nondiscrimination and focus exclusively on merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration distinction: scholarships (state) vs fellowships (national)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarships should be assigned by State quotas; fellowships should be awarded on a national, not a State, basis and administered nationally as National Research Council Fellowships are administered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether or not a National Scientific Research Foundation is established, the National Research Council is judged the best agency to administer the fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship stipend and tuition support
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship stipends should be fixed by the awarding agency on a scale up to $100 monthly, plus payments for tuition and other fees up to a maximum of $500 annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarding agency determines exact stipend within these maxima.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insistence on high-grade work and termination policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the whole plan there should run an insistence upon high-grade work by the holder; otherwise the fellowship or scholarship shall be terminated by the awarding agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awarding agency has authority to terminate awards for insufficient academic/work performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for continuance of awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Both scholarships and fellowships shall be held upon the following conditions: (a) Continuance of good health. (b) Continuance of good behavior. (c) Scientific progress at the level of the best 25 percent of former students in the scientific departments primarily concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit continuance requirements; failure on these grounds may trigger termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of awards (tenure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarships shall be tenable for 4 academic years or the equivalent. Fellowships shall be tenable for the duration of graduate studies leading to the doctoral degree, up to a maximum of 3 academic years or the equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tenure limits define maximum periods for which awards may be held.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dropout and alternate policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Scholar or Fellow drops out for failure or other reasons, his scholarship or fellowship should lapse. Alternates should not be appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No replacement or alternates are to be appointed for dropouts under this plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution eligibility and transfer rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarships and fellowships should be valid for any college or university within the United States of the holder’s choice, subject to the advice and consent of the awarding agency concerning relevant facilities for scientific work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With the consent of the awarding agency, a Scholar or Fellow may change the location of his work to another institution judged better suited to his scientific development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship eligibility openness
rubrics_metrics.description: National Science Reserve Scholars should be eligible to appointment as National Science Reserve Fellows, but appointments to the fellowships should not be restricted to the National Science Reserve Scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships should be open to competition from all pre-doctoral science students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synchronized commencement of awards
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended that the award of the scholarships and of the fellowships be commenced simultaneously, or approximately so, to the full annual number in each category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative planning should aim for concurrent launch of both programs at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing research into selection methods and employment opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Agency in charge of the scholarships and fellowships should carry on continuing research into methods of selection and continuing study of unfolding opportunities (and the reverse) for employment in science and technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing evaluation and adaptation of selection methods and employment tracking is required to keep the program effective and up-to-date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and ordering of promising servicemembers as students
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare lists of promising students of science and technology among servicemembers and, when militarily feasible, order these talented students by name to duty as students for fully independent, integrated scientific study of civilian-grade quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include students at all levels (college freshman to post-doctoral) and former teachers; do not rely on volunteer requests; the Research Board for National Security could set up the discovery machinery; estimate possibly no more than 100,000 involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-interference by commanders in student reassignment
rubrics_metrics.description: This should be adopted as the considered policy of the armed services and no desire of a commanding officer to retain a potential scientist for his usefulness on the spot should be allowed to interfere with the operation of the policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy must override local command preferences to secure reassignment of promising talent to student duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality standards for 'Army universities' instruction abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses of study for soldiers abroad, including science and technology, must be the best and most up-to-date possible and shall include adequate laboratory work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Army university instruction should be supplemented by bringing fresh, up-to-date instructors from universities, technical schools, and industry to teach overseas; integrate training with modern industry and technology problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI Bill: special advisory committee for veterans' scientific talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint a special advisory committee of scientists to assist administrators of the GI Bill to discover and direct the counseling of veterans who have marked scientific talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee would help identify veterans deserving extended education support beyond the standard one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI Bill: state/regional advising and counseling services
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish an adequate advising and counseling service in each State or region to guide veterans with scientific potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These services should identify and advise veterans during their initial year of government-supported education and testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: GI Bill: provision of complete scientific education for selected veterans
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a complete scientific education at Government expense for a group selected on the basis of the educational record of the first year and such other tests as may be necessary—the length of this education to be determined, on the merits of each case, by the special advisory committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend a selective process as rigorous as that provided under the main plan; favor qualitative selection by ability rather than fixed quotas or service length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to amend GI Bill for ability-based selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Advise new legislation authorizing administrators to select, as an estimate, possibly 5,000 veterans of each age group for scientific education at Government expense irrespective of length of military service and up to a total of 6 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer standards of scientific and technological ability as limiting factors rather than fixed numerical quotas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colleges/universities must be flexible with veterans
rubrics_metrics.description: Colleges, universities, and technical schools should be extremely flexible and broad-minded in handling returning veterans who may not meet usual formal requirements; they must devise ways of building on partial but detailed technical training received in service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should shorten requirements where possible, use special institutions or vocational schools, and avoid rigid rules that would lose talented veterans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for over-age high school students and War Service Schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide special programs for over-age high school students (returning veterans and workers), such as War Service Schools with accelerated courses and full-calendar utilization, granting credit for work completed in the Armed Forces Institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional War Service Schools, dedicated buildings in large cities, and flexible secondary programs should be used to attract veterans to complete high school and become eligible for college scholarship programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of service education records and USAFI procedures for credit
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete educational record established while in the service should be recorded on USAFI No. 47 and returned to the secondary school for evaluation and award of credit toward graduation; veterans who do not file USAFI credit application should use a certified copy of their separation record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General Educational Development Tests (GED) are helpful in determining grade level for resumption of civilian education; these procedures facilitate continuance to college for qualified persons.
